stem.text: The amount of water in a storage tank is modeled by a differentiable function W of time t, measured in hours, whose rate of change is \( W'(t) = - \frac{20 e^{- \frac{t}{12}}}{3} \) hundreds of gallons per hour, for \( 0 \le t \le 36 \). Using a calculator, find \( W'(6) \), showing the setup, and interpret the value in the context of the problem with correct units. Give the value correct to three decimal places.

answer_key.label: \( W'(6) = -4.044 \), so at time t = 6 hours the amount of water in the tank is decreasing at a rate of 4.044 hundreds of gallons per hour.

worked_solution.text: With a calculator, \( W'(6) = -4.044 \) to three decimal places.
worked_solution.rule_named: evaluate the derivative at the instant

worked_solution.text: The value is negative, so at time t = 6 hours the amount of water in the tank is decreasing at a rate of 4.044 hundreds of gallons per hour.
worked_solution.rule_named: sign of the rate gives the direction of change

options.label: \( W'(6) = -4.044 \), so at time t = 6 hours the amount of water in the tank is decreasing at a rate of 4.044 hours per hundred gallons.
options.derivation: the units assembled the wrong way round, time units over the units of the quantity

options.label: \( W'(6) = -4.044 \), so when the amount of water in the tank is 6 hundreds of gallons it is decreasing at a rate of 4.044 hundreds of gallons per hour.
options.derivation: the independent variable never named, so the input is read as a value of the quantity rather than a time

options.label: \( W'(6) = -4.044 \), so at time t = 6 hours the amount of water in the tank is moving with a velocity of -4.044 hundreds of gallons per hour.
options.derivation: the rate of change of a non-motion quantity called a velocity
